_comment: Reference standard for target verdicts. Every consuming repository has its own small
implementation of the refusal rule; each proves itself against THESE vectors.
Independent implementations agreeing on a published reference set is a stronger
property than identical copies of one file, and it is the argument this platform
already makes for its shared scoring engine.
Every credential below is FABRICATED. The JWTs are unsigned, carry only a `ref`
claim, and authenticate nothing. No real key, token or environment file may ever
N1-D3: ovtjqkbvyhsfqzexhuup is the REAL isolated Learning demo project. A project
ref is public (see README) -- only credentials are fabricated, and every JWT here
still is. It appears on the allowlist so these vectors prove the actual demo target
is permitted while production and every retired project stay refused.

cases.name: N1-D2 an opaque demo publishable key contributes no ref and does not poison a clean target
cases._note: An `sb_publishable_` key carries no claims. It must not be read as a project ref -- not even a wrong one. Paired with an allowlisted target the verdict is PERMIT, which is only reachable if the opaque key contributed nothing. Its companion vector sends a JWT-shaped demo key carrying a production ref through the same variable and is REFUSED, so the pair proves the guard reads claims where they exist and invents none where they do not.
